# Check coverage: what each guard prevents, and what it is blind to

Each rule is "prevented by" a named check. A blind spot is a way the rule can be broken
without that check noticing; reviewers cover blind spots by hand. Edit `.agents/checks.toml`
(factory-managed) or `.agents/checks.local.toml` (repo-owned), then run `julia scripts/gen.jl`.

| No destructive git/rm commands, no pushes or GitHub actions without the user, no writes outside the repo root, no modelled writes to T3 protected paths (without the user's FACTORY_ALLOW_T3=1), only read-only commands inside the read-only roots of .agents/factory.toml | `.claude/hooks/bash_guard.sh` | hook PreToolUse(Bash|Monitor) | `scripts/test/test_hooks.jl` | commands built at runtime: aliases, functions, scripts, julia/python -e, `sh -c '...'`/`bash -c` strings and arguments to tools that run commands (`git -c alias.x='!...'`, `make` recipes); a command NAME that is an expansion (`$X`, `$(...)`, backticks, `${IFS}`) and `eval` are blocked; write targets held in variables (`> "$f"`, `cp a "$D"`) are not resolved and pass; only `$HOME` and `$TMPDIR` (the hook's own value) are expanded; the read-only allowlist trusts its tools (`less` can run `!cmd`; `git log/diff --output=f`, `rg --pre`, `git -c core.pager=...`); subshells, `popd` and `cd -` are not unwound, so `(cd root && ls); make` counts `make` as inside the root (a false positive, never a bypass); a write target held in a variable, built at runtime or reached through a symlink is not matched; `mkdir` and `touch` of a directory are not checked as directory targets; targets read from stdin (`find . \| xargs rm`) are not seen; others (`stdbuf`, `chroot`, `parallel`, `watch`, `script`, `flock`, `ssh`) hide the command they run; a sourced library (`_lib.sh`, `_bash_guard_lib.sh`, `_read_only_roots.sh`, `_bash_guard_cmd.sh`, `_bash_guard_write.sh`) that is missing blocks; leading tabs stripped for `<<-`), never at WORD followed by `)` (0.4.0 review round 2: inside "$(...)" bash ends the body there but zsh reads on to the bare WORD line and runs what follows, so that line is denied; the `)` on its own line after WORD is read alike); a lenient terminator (trailing blanks, a CR, leading blanks, a top-level `WORD)`) is a body line, as in bash, so that body is never terminated and is checked as commands, like any unterminated body: `pkill` or a denied write in it is refused (0.4.0 review B1: ending the body there let a later body line open a second heredoc that hid the lines bash runs);
